markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

Three starting-point insights guide this proposal. First, SASRec already models causal sequence dependencies; a small residual permits an interpretable intervention. Its benefit must be established against unchanged SASRec. Second, Electronics has 14.95% wrong rankings and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin. These training diagnostics motivate better discrimination but do not establish validation gains. Third, users value recent intent and repeated specific preferences. Broad associations and speculative equipment upgrades reveal insufficient behavioral support, although histories cannot establish compatibility.

Three literature insights suggest complementary directions. [ICSRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.14318) transfers supervision between subsequences sharing targets. Shared behavior supplies evidence, rather than verified intent. [SComGNN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.02130) distinguishes relevance from similarity in complementary relationships. Directed historical successors therefore offer a useful signal beyond content resemblance. [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) motivates multiple negatives and calibrated BCE. Objective improvements remain a separate hypothesis from architectural improvements.

### Framework and alternatives

| Direction | Minimal idea | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal preference | Gate between short and long causal pooling | Pooling may blur specific intent |
| Behavioral evidence | **Recent-anchor transition lift residual** | Sparse edges and confounding |
| Ranking objective | Replace single-negative BCE with gBCE | False negatives and runtime |

Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Detailed positive and negative assessments accompany the implementation notes.

| Idea | Scores |
|---|---|
| Two-window pooling | 3/6/7/5/3 |
| Transition lift residual | **4/7/7/6/4** |
| Multi-negative gBCE | 2/7/5/8/4 |

### Selected algorithm

At 0% progress, select the transition lift residual: a small, testable extension of the previous directed-residual inspiration. Replace its learned transition embeddings with a fixed, shrunk population transition statistic, and aggregate evidence across a recent suffix. This isolates whether supported successor evidence helps before adding representation learning.

Count adjacent transitions once per training user and ordered pair. Compute smoothed transition lift relative to target popularity. Add only positive, bounded lift, weighted by edge support and exponentially decaying anchor recency; divide by total anchor weight, including unsupported anchors. Learn one bounded residual amplitude per dataset, initialized near zero.

This explicitly targets two user failures: broad associations outranking recent intent, and specialized upgrades recommended without behavioral support. Repeated population successors provide limited evidence for plausible next actions; they cannot verify ownership, dimensions, compatibility, or satisfied needs. The model-facing target is Electronics’ weak margin tail.

Preserve all four routes, seeds, splits, baseline training settings, and diagnostic interfaces. Compare baseline, last-anchor lift, and recent-suffix lift with matched validation opportunities within the shared budget. Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Report edge coverage, margin changes, and simulator mismatch feedback separately; no improvement is established.

idea.description: Add a bounded recent-anchor transition-lift residual to each dataset's SASRec. Construct distinct-user directed adjacent-transition counts from training histories, shrink conditional probabilities toward transition-target popularity, and aggregate positive lift over the last five causal anchors. Learn only one bounded amplitude per dataset. Unlike the previous inspiration, this proposal uses fixed count-derived transition scores instead of separate learned source/target embeddings and a feature-conditioned gate.
idea.motivation: The residual explicitly targets broad associations outranking recent intent and speculative specialized upgrades lacking behavioral support. Recent directed successors provide a limited behavioral reason to recommend an item now. They do not prove compatibility, equipment ownership, replacement needs, or purchase completion. Quantitatively, the intervention targets weak positive–negative separation, especially Electronics' 14.95% wrong-ranking rate and negative lower-tail margin. These diagnostics justify investigation, not a claim of higher validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes:
Algorithm specification: For each dataset, count c(i,j) once per training user who exhibits adjacent pair (i,j). Let C(i)=sum_j c(i,j), T(j)=sum_i c(i,j), and p0(j)=(T(j)+1)/(sum_j T(j)+N), over real catalog items. C(i) counts user-edge incidences, not distinct source users. Define p(j|i)=(c(i,j)+20*p0(j))/(C(i)+20). For observed edges, define r(i,j)=C(i)/(C(i)+10) * c(i,j)/(c(i,j)+3) * clip(log(p(j|i)/p0(j)),0,2). Set r=0 for unobserved edges and padding. Initial constants are engineering defaults, not estimated optima.

At position t, use up to five nonpadding anchors ending at t, with weights 2^(-age/2). The residual is their weighted mean r, dividing by all anchor weights rather than only supported anchors. This prevents a single weakly covered anchor from receiving full weight. Repeated anchors retain their recency-weighted contributions; no semantic labels are inferred. Score s(t,j)=SASRecScore(t,j)+a*residual(t,j), where a=2*sigmoid(theta), initialized to 0.01. The total additive contribution is bounded by 4. Preserve the baseline optimizer, negative sampler and loss initially; include theta in the optimizer. Positive-only lift cannot directly penalize unsupported recommendations, so it may fail to displace them when supported alternatives are absent. Counts remain susceptible to popularity and confounding despite lift normalization.

Training-only population counts can use all training histories; per-position anchors must use only the causal prefix through that position. Never use validation or test interactions in counts. Store sorted sparse edge keys and residual values as model buffers; look up keys i*(N+1)+j using int64 searchsorted with explicit bounds and exact-match checks. Handle empty tables. Compute recent-anchor scores sequentially or in chunks to avoid a B*L*K*5 allocation. Store the exact item mapping, counts/statistics, architecture configuration and checkpoints beneath the trial directory.

Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four category routes and int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')). Use one GPU. Update the predictor writer to emit the identical model class and sparse scoring implementation. Keep log2feats(sequence) tensor-valued by concatenating the SASRec state with five anchor-ID channels, stored in float64 to preserve integer IDs; verify runtime ID round trips, and cast the hidden-state slice back to the model dtype before scoring. Alternatively use a structured feature object only if every existing consumer is adapted consistently. Keep view.item_emb pointing to the SASRec item table, view.model pointing to the actual complete module, and score all diagnostic margins through view.predict_score. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, with loader batches (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Category metadata breakdowns must be marked unavailable; do not synthesize ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores, or simulator traits. Embedding similarity measures the backbone table and cannot diagnose the count residual itself.

Assessments, with higher difficulty indicating greater implementation effort:
1. Two-window causal pooling: Originality 3/10 (+ lightweight synthesis of temporal views; − multiscale interests are established). Potential 6/10 (+ can adapt to changing intent; − fixed windows are coarse). User alignment 7/10 (+ emphasizes current and sustained preferences; − supplies no equipment evidence). Model alignment 5/10 (+ may improve confusing states; − no direct evidence it fixes margin tails). Difficulty 3/10 (+ pooling and a gate are small additions; − causal masking and export still need care).
2. Recent-anchor transition lift: Originality 4/10 (+ combines multi-anchor support, shrinkage and bounded fallback; − transition and lift models are longstanding). Potential 7/10 (+ isolates an interpretable population-evidence hypothesis; − coverage can be poor). User alignment 7/10 (+ prioritizes recent supported successors over broad association and unsupported upgrades; − observed successors do not verify practical suitability). Model alignment 6/10 (+ directly changes confusing candidate orderings; − can raise false positives and does not improve unsupported edges). Difficulty 4/10 (+ only one learned scalar beyond SASRec; − sparse lookup, causal anchors and full-catalog parity need integration).
3. Multi-negative gBCE: Originality 2/10 (+ a clean objective control; − directly follows published machinery). Potential 7/10 (+ stronger sampled discrimination may transfer across datasets; − gains depend on sampling and compute). User alignment 5/10 (+ better ranking could increase clear matches; − no explicit mechanism for current intent or unsupported equipment). Model alignment 8/10 (+ directly addresses weak sampled separation; − diagnostic negatives need not reflect validation candidates). Difficulty 4/10 (+ published loss is compact; − multiple-negative memory and exclusions require care).

Prespecify three variants: unchanged SASRec, last-anchor count residual, and five-anchor count residual. Allocate at most 12,000 GPU-seconds per variant across all four datasets, split equally; reserve 7,200 seconds for diagnostics, debugging and failures. Count every GPU cost toward 43,200 seconds. Each category stops at 200 epochs or 3,000 GPU-seconds. Save matched checkpoints at 1,000, 2,000 and 3,000 seconds per category, reusing completed checkpoints when training ends earlier. Select the four-category checkpoint bundle solely by pinned macro validation HR@10; exact ties prefer baseline, then last-anchor, then earlier checkpoints. If baseline runtime requires changing the schedule, record one revision before running comparisons. Do not launch the other proposed ideas within this allocation.

Verify exported versus training candidate scores and candidate versus chunked full-catalog scores, covering all routes, padding, truncation, candidate broadcasting and reloads. Require float32 scorer agreement within atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 and resolve top-10 disagreements. Track edge coverage, added-score magnitude, original margin statistics, and source/target popularity strata. Run the required twenty-user unseen-item simulator protocol, but select only by the unchanged host validation metric. The supplied 0.5287 inspiration score is historical context; it is not evidence for this new algorithm.
idea.pseudocode:
# Specification for integration into the supplied per-dataset baseline.
# Do not replace preprocessing, routing, evaluator, or baseline loss.

for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    counts = Counter()
    for history in training_histories[dataset].values():
        for i, j in set(zip(history[:-1], history[1:])):
            if i != 0 and j != 0:
                counts[i, j] += 1

    source = sum_counts_by_source(counts)
    target = sum_counts_by_target(counts)
    p0 = (target + 1) / (sum(target) + num_real_items)
    edges = {}
    for (i, j), c in counts.items():
        conditional = (c + 20 * p0[j]) / (source[i] + 20)
        lift = clip(log(conditional / p0[j]), 0, 2)
        edges[i, j] = source[i] / (source[i] + 10) * c / (c + 3) * lift

    model = BaselineSASRecWithSparseResidual(edges)
    model.theta = Parameter(logit(0.01 / 2.0))

    def score(hidden, causal_anchor_ids, candidates):
        numerator = zeros_like_candidate_scores(hidden, candidates)
        denominator = zeros_like_position_counts(hidden)
        for age in range(5):
            anchor = causal_anchor_ids[..., age]
            weight = (2 ** (-age / 2)) * (anchor != 0)
            numerator += broadcast(weight) * sparse_lookup(edges, anchor, candidates, default=0)
            denominator += weight
        residual = numerator / broadcast(clamp_min(denominator, 1e-8))
        return baseline_dot_score(hidden, candidates) + 2 * sigmoid(model.theta) * residual

    for _, sequence, positive, negative in train_loader:
        hidden = model.backbone.log2feats(sequence)
        anchors = causal_last_nonpadding_items(sequence, maximum=5)
        valid = (sequence != 0) & (positive != 0)
        positive_score = score(hidden, anchors, positive)
        negative_score = score(hidden, anchors, negative)
        loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(positive_score, negative_score, valid)
        optimize(loss)
        respect_prespecified_compute_and_checkpoint_schedule()

    save_model_sparse_buffers_mapping_and_config_under_trial_directory()
    write_predictor_with_identical_architecture_and_scoring()
    verify_export_and_full_catalog_parity()

# Compare baseline, last-anchor, and five-anchor variants only.
# Run adapted DiagnosisProbe through the complete scorer.
# Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Multi-anchor aggregation with explicit support shrinkage provides a precise, interpretable variation on the earlier learned directed residual.
originality.negative: Directed transition counts, popularity lift, recency weighting and residual blending are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Creates a small controlled experiment on when population successor evidence complements personal causal sequence representations.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transition coverage, confounding and unknown compatibility limit both coverage and practical interpretation.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires fixed sparse statistics and one learned scalar per dataset rather than additional embedding tables.
code_difficulty.negative: Sparse candidate lookup, causal anchor alignment, diagnostic feature compatibility and predictor parity require careful integration.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention backbone and candidate dot-product scoring.
limitations: Does not explicitly require population transition evidence for a recommendation.

related_work.title: Intent Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Uses subsequences and shared targets to obtain intent-related supervision without explicit intent labels.
limitations: Shared targets do not establish identical intent or functional compatibility.

related_work.title: SComGNN
contributions: Motivates distinguishing relevance and dissimilarity when modeling complementary relationships.
limitations: Its relation modeling does not establish that adjacent purchases in this benchmark are true complements.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Addresses sampling-related overconfidence using multiple negatives and generalized binary cross-entropy.
limitations: Does not establish Electronics-specific causation or gains under this pinned four-dataset evaluation.
